sanskrit: eṣa dhātā vidhātā ca siddhir atra pratiṣṭhitā yam āha kṛṣṇo dāśārhaḥ sa naḥ senāpatiḥ kṣamaḥ bravītu vadatāṃ śreṣṭho niśā samativartate
english: He is the creator and the ordainer; success is established here. Whom Kṛṣṇa of the Dāśārha clan has named — he is fit to be our commander. Let the best among speakers speak; the night is passing.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā kṛṣṇasya vaśavartinam rātriśeṣe vyatikrānte prayāsyāmo raṇājiram adhivāsitaśastrāś ca kṛtakautukamaṅgalāḥ
english: Then, having installed as commander one who follows Kṛṣṇa's will, when the remainder of the night has passed, we shall march to the battlefield — our weapons consecrated and auspicious rites performed with joy.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ abravīt puṇḍarīkākṣo dhanaṃjayam avekṣya ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard those words of the wise Dharma-king, the lotus-eyed one, glancing toward Dhanañjaya, spoke.

sanskrit: mamāpy ete mahārāja bhavadbhir ya udāhṛtāḥ netāras tava senāyāḥ śūrā vikrāntayodhinaḥ sarva ete samarthā hi tava śatrūn pramarditum
english: These leaders of your army whom you have named, O great king — they are heroes, mighty warriors. All of them are capable of crushing your enemies.

sanskrit: indrasyāpi bhayaṃ hy ete janayeyur mahāhave kiṃ punar dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ lubdhānāṃ pāpacetasām
english: In great battle, these men could strike fear even in Indra himself — what then of the greedy, evil-minded sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra?

sanskrit: mayāpi hi mahābāho tvatpriyārtham ariṃdama kṛto yatno mahāṃs tatra śamaḥ syād iti bhārata dharmasya gatam ānṛṇyaṃ na sma vācyā vivakṣatām
english: I too, O mighty-armed slayer of foes, made great effort for your sake — hoping there might be peace, O Bhārata. The debt of dharma has been paid; those who wish to speak cannot reproach us.

sanskrit: kṛtārthaṃ manyate bālaḥ so ''tmānam avicakṣaṇaḥ dhārtarāṣṭro balasthaṃ ca manyate ''tmānam āturaḥ
english: That childish, unwise Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son considers himself accomplished. The afflicted one considers himself strong — a fool's self-delusion.

sanskrit: yujyatāṃ vāhinī sādhu vadhasādhyā hi te matāḥ na dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ śakṣyanti sthātuṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanaṃjayam
english: Let the army be marshalled well — for in my judgment those foes are to be subdued by slaughter. The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will not be able to stand firm when they behold Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ ca saṃkruddhaṃ yamau cāpi yamopamau yuyudhānadvitīyaṃ ca dhṛṣṭadyumnam amarṣaṇam
english: And furious Bhīmasena, and the twins who are like Yama himself, and Yuyudhāna as his second, and the wrathful Dhṛṣṭadyumna —

sanskrit: abhimanyuṃ draupadeyān virāṭadrupadāv api akṣauhiṇīpatīṃś cānyān narendrān dṛḍhavikramān
english: Abhimanyu, the sons of Draupadī, Virāṭa and Drupada as well, and the other lords of akshauhini divisions — kings of firm valor —

sanskrit: sāravad balam asmākaṃ duṣpradharṣaṃ durāsadam dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ saṃkhye vadhiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Our army, full of essence and irresistible, impregnable — without doubt it will slay the Dhṛtarāṣṭra forces in battle.

sanskrit: evam ukte tu kṛṣṇena saṃprahṛṣyan narottamāḥ teṣāṃ prahṛṣṭamanasāṃ nādaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: When Kṛṣṇa had spoken thus, the foremost of men rejoiced greatly; and from those whose hearts were delighted a great roar arose.

sanskrit: yoga ity atha sainyānāṃ tvaratāṃ saṃpradhāvatām hayavāraṇaśabdaś ca nemighoṣaś ca sarvaśaḥ śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣas tumulaḥ sarvato 'bhavat
english: "To arms!" — and the armies rushed forward in haste. The cries of horses and elephants, the clatter of wheel-rims from every direction, the tumultuous blast of conches and kettledrums arose on all sides.

sanskrit: prayāsyatāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ sasainyānāṃ samantataḥ gaṅgeva pūrṇā durdharṣā samadṛśyata vāhinī
english: As the Pāṇḍavas set forth with their armies in every direction, the host appeared like the Gaṅgā in flood — full and irresistible.

sanskrit: agrānīke bhīmaseno mādrīputrau ca daṃśitau saubhadro draupadeyāś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ prabhadrakāś ca pāñcālā bhīmasenamukhā yayuḥ
english: In the vanguard marched Bhīmasena and the armored sons of Mādrī, Subhadrā's son and the sons of Draupadī, Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, and the Prabhadrakas and Pāñcālas — all with Bhīmasena at their head.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdaḥ samabhavat samudrasyeva parvaṇi hṛṣṭānāṃ saṃprayātānāṃ ghoṣo divam ivāspṛśat
english: Then a sound arose like the ocean at high tide; the clamor of the joyful marching host seemed to touch the sky.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭā daṃśitā yodhāḥ parānīkavidāraṇāḥ teṣāṃ madhye yayau rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Joyful and armored, those warriors, destroyers of enemy ranks, marched; and in their midst went the king, Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: śakaṭāpaṇaveśāś ca yānayugyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ kośayantrāyudhaṃ caiva ye ca vaidyāś cikitsakāḥ
english: The wagon-shops and market stalls, all manner of conveyances and draft animals, the treasury, siege-engines and weapons, as well as physicians and healers —

sanskrit: phalgu yac ca balaṃ kiṃ cit tathaiva kṛśadurbalam tat saṃgṛhya yayau rājā ye cāpi paricārakāḥ
english: Whatever weak or feeble auxiliary force there was, however lean and infirm — the king gathered all of it, together with the attendants and camp-followers, and marched on.

sanskrit: upaplavye tu pāñcālī draupadī satyavādinī saha strībhir nivavṛte dāsīdāsasamāvṛtā
english: But at Upaplavya, the Pāñcālī Draupadī, the truth-speaker, remained behind with the other women, surrounded by her maidservants and male servants.

sanskrit: kṛtvā mūlapratīkārān gulmaiḥ sthāvarajaṅgamaiḥ skandhāvāreṇa mahatā prayayuḥ pāṇḍunandanāḥ
english: Having made arrangements for the base camp with stationary and mobile guard detachments, the sons of Pāṇḍu marched forth with a great cantonment-army.

sanskrit: dadato gāṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca brāhmaṇair abhisaṃvṛtāḥ stūyamānā yayū rājan rathair maṇivibhūṣitaiḥ
english: Bestowing cows and gold, surrounded by brahmins who chanted their praises, they marched, O king, in chariots adorned with jewels.

sanskrit: kekayā dhṛṣṭaketuś ca putraḥ kāśyasya cābhibhūḥ śreṇimān vasudānaś ca śikhaṇḍī cāparājitaḥ
english: The Kekayas, Dhṛṣṭaketu, the son of the king of Kāśi named Abhibhū, Śreṇimān, Vasudāna, and the unvanquished Śikhaṇḍī —

sanskrit: hṛṣṭās tuṣṭāḥ kavacinaḥ saśastrāḥ samalaṃkṛtāḥ rājānam anvayuḥ sarve parivārya yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Joyful and content, clad in armor, armed and adorned, all of them followed the king, surrounding Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: jaghanārdhe virāṭaś ca yajñasenaś ca somakiḥ sudharmā kuntibhojaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cātmajāḥ
english: In the rear guard were Virāṭa, Yajñasena the Somaka, Sudharma, Kuntibhoja, and the sons of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: rathāyutāni catvāri hayāḥ pañcaguṇās tataḥ pattisainyaṃ daśaguṇaṃ sādinām ayutāni ṣaṭ
english: Four times ten thousand chariots, horses five times as many, infantry ten times that number, and sixty thousand cavalry.

sanskrit: anādhṛṣṭiś cekitānaś cedirājo 'tha sātyakiḥ parivārya yayuḥ sarve vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Anādhṛṣṭi, Cekitāna, the king of the Cedis, and Sātyaki — all of them marched surrounding Vāsudeva and Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: āsādya tu kurukṣetraṃ vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ pāṇḍavāḥ samadṛśyanta nardanto vṛṣabhā iva
english: Having reached Kurukṣetra, the Pāṇḍavas appeared with their armies arrayed and ready to strike, roaring like bulls.

sanskrit: te 'vagāhya kurukṣetraṃ śaṅkhān dadhmur ariṃdamāḥ tathaiva dadhmatuḥ śaṅkhau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Those slayers of foes, having entered Kurukṣetra, blew their conches; and likewise Vāsudeva and Dhanañjaya both blew their conches.

sanskrit: pāñcajanyasya nirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ niśamya sarvasainyāni samahṛṣyanta sarvaśaḥ
english: Hearing the blast of the Pāñcajanya conch, like the crack of a thunderbolt, all the armies thrilled with joy on every side.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhisaṃsṛṣṭaḥ siṃhanādas tarasvinām pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca sāgarāṃś cānvanādayat
english: The lion-roars of those swift warriors, mingled with the sound of conches and kettledrums, made the earth, the sky, and the oceans resound in echo.

sanskrit: tato deśe same snigdhe prabhūtayavasendhane niveśayām āsa tadā senāṃ rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then king Yudhiṣṭhira encamped his army in a level, pleasant region, rich in barley, fodder, and fuel.

sanskrit: parihṛtya śmaśānāni devatāyatanāni ca āśramāṃś ca maharṣīṇāṃ tīrthāny āyatanāni ca
english: Avoiding cremation grounds and temples of the gods, the hermitages of great sages, sacred fords, and holy sites —

sanskrit: madhurānūṣare deśe śive puṇye mahīpatiḥ niveśaṃ kārayām āsa kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: — in a pleasant, lightly saline tract, auspicious and holy, the lord of the earth, Yudhiṣṭhira son of Kuntī, had the camp laid out.

sanskrit: tataś ca punar utthāya sukhī viśrāntavāhanaḥ prayayau pṛthivīpālair vṛtaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Then, rising again, at ease and with rested mounts, he marched forward, surrounded by kings in their hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: vidrāvya śataśo gulmān dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainikān paryakrāmat samantāc ca pārthena saha keśavaḥ
english: Routing hundreds of outpost detachments of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's soldiers, Keśava together with Pārtha ranged about on all sides.

sanskrit: śibiraṃ māpayām āsa dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ sātyakiś ca rathodāro yuyudhānaḥ pratāpavān
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, son of Pṛṣata, and the noble chariot-warrior Sātyaki — the valiant Yuyudhāna — measured out and marked the camp.

sanskrit: āsādya saritaṃ puṇyāṃ kurukṣetre hiraṇvatīm sūpatīrthāṃ śucijalāṃ śarkarāpaṅkavarjitām
english: Having reached the sacred river Hiraṇvatī in Kurukṣetra — blessed with good fords, with pure water, free of gravel and mire —

sanskrit: khānayām āsa parikhāṃ keśavas tatra bhārata guptyartham api cādiśya balaṃ tatra nyaveśayat
english: — there, O Bhārata, Keśava had a moat dug for protection, and, having stationed guards, he settled the army in that place.

sanskrit: vidhir yaḥ śibirasyāsīt pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām tadvidhāni narendrāṇāṃ kārayām āsa keśavaḥ
english: Whatever the arrangement of the camp had been for the great-souled Pāṇḍavas — Keśava had the camps of all the kings laid out in the same manner.

sanskrit: prabhūtajalakāṣṭhāni durādharṣatarāṇi ca bhakṣyabhojyopapannāni śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Abundantly supplied with water and firewood, made even more difficult to assail, stocked with food and provisions — by the hundreds and thousands —

sanskrit: śibirāṇi mahārhāṇi rājñāṃ tatra pṛthak pṛthak vimānānīva rājendra niviṣṭāni mahītale
english: — the splendid camps of the kings were pitched there, each separately from the others, like celestial palaces set down upon the earth, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: tatrāsañ śilpinaḥ prājñāḥ śataśo dattavetanāḥ sarvopakaraṇair yuktā vaidyāś ca suviśāradāḥ
english: There were skilled craftsmen by the hundreds, paid their wages, furnished with all implements, and physicians highly expert in their art.

sanskrit: jyādhanurvarmaśastrāṇāṃ tathaiva madhusarpiṣoḥ sasarja rasapāṃsūnāṃ rāśayaḥ parvatopamāḥ
english: Heaps like mountains were amassed — of bowstrings, bows, armor, and weapons, and likewise of honey, clarified butter, medicinal juices, and powders.

sanskrit: bahūdakaṃ suyavasaṃ tuṣāṅgārasamanvitam śibire śibire rājā saṃcakāra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Plentiful water, good fodder, chaff and charcoal — king Yudhiṣṭhira caused all of this to be gathered in camp after camp.

sanskrit: mahāyantrāṇi nārācās tomararṣṭiparaśvadhāḥ dhanūṃṣi kavacādīni hṛdy abhūvan nṛṇāṃ tadā
english: Great siege-engines, iron arrows, javelins, lances, battle-axes, bows, armor and the rest — all of these were close to the hearts of the men in that hour.

sanskrit: gajāḥ kaṅkaṭasaṃnāhā lohavarmottaracchadāḥ adṛśyaṃs tatra giryābhāḥ sahasraśatayodhinaḥ
english: Elephants harnessed in mail-armor, covered with iron-plate barding, were seen there — mountain-like, each capable of fighting hundreds and thousands of foes.

sanskrit: niviṣṭān pāṇḍavāṃs tatra jñātvā mitrāṇi bhārata abhisasrur yathoddeśaṃ sabalāḥ sahavāhanāḥ
english: Learning that the Pāṇḍavas were encamped there, O Bhārata, their allies came streaming in as appointed, with their forces and vehicles.

sanskrit: caritabrahmacaryās te somapā bhūridakṣiṇāḥ jayāya pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ samājagmur mahīkṣitaḥ
english: Those kings who had observed celibacy, drunken the soma, and performed sacrifices with lavish gifts came together for the victory of the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca yudhiṣṭhiraṃ sahānīkam upayāntaṃ yuyutsayā saṃniviṣṭaṃ kurukṣetre vāsudevena pālitam
english: Janamejaya said: Yudhiṣṭhira approaching with his army, eager for battle, encamped at Kurukṣetra, protected by Vāsudeva —

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadābhyāṃ ca saputrābhyāṃ samanvitam kekayair vṛṣṇibhiś caiva pārthivaiḥ śataśo vṛtam
english: — accompanied by Virāṭa and Drupada with their sons, surrounded by the Kekayas and the Vṛṣṇis, and by hundreds of kings —

sanskrit: mahendram iva cādityair abhiguptaṃ mahārathaiḥ śrutvā duryodhano rājā kiṃ kāryaṃ pratyapadyata
english: — guarded by great chariot-warriors like Mahendra guarded by the Ādityas — hearing of this, what course of action did king Duryodhana adopt?

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa tapodhana saṃbhrame tumule tasmin yadāsīt kurujāṅgale
english: This I wish to hear in full detail, O ascetic sage — what transpired in that tumult and commotion on the Kuru plain.

sanskrit: vyathayeyur hi devānāṃ senām api samāgame pāṇḍavā vāsudevaś ca virāṭadrupadau tathā
english: For in battle the Pāṇḍavas, Vāsudeva, and likewise Virāṭa and Drupada could torment even the army of the gods when they are assembled.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pāñcālyaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ yuyudhānaś ca vikrānto devair api durāsadaḥ
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna of the Pāñcālas, and Śikhaṇḍī the great chariot-warrior, and the valiant Yuyudhāna — unapproachable even by the gods.

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa tapodhana kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yad yad āsīd viceṣṭitam
english: All of this I wish to hear in full, O ascetic sage — whatever the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas did and how they each conducted themselves.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pratiyāte tu dāśārhe rājā duryodhanas tadā karṇaṃ duḥśāsanaṃ caiva śakuniṃ cābravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the Dāśārha hero had departed, king Duryodhana then spoke this to Karṇa, Duḥśāsana, and Śakuni:

sanskrit: akṛtenaiva kāryeṇa gataḥ pārthān adhokṣajaḥ sa enān manyunāviṣṭo dhruvaṃ vakṣyaty asaṃśayam
english: "Adhokṣaja has gone to the Pārthas with the mission unaccomplished. Filled with anger at them, he will certainly incite them — there is no doubt."

sanskrit: iṣṭo hi vāsudevasya pāṇḍavair mama vigrahaḥ bhīmasenārjunau caiva dāśārhasya mate sthitau
english: "For conflict with me is dear to Vāsudeva's Pāṇḍavas; both Bhīmasena and Arjuna stand in agreement with the Dāśārha's counsel."

sanskrit: ajātaśatrur apy adya bhīmārjunavaśānugaḥ nikṛtaś ca mayā pūrvaṃ saha sarvaiḥ sahodaraiḥ
english: "Even Ajātaśatru today follows the will of Bhīma and Arjuna; and he was previously deceived by me along with all my brothers."

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadau caiva kṛtavairau mayā saha tau ca senāpraṇetārau vāsudevavaśānugau
english: "Virāṭa and Drupada too have been made enemies of mine, and they are the leaders of that army, followers of Vāsudeva's will."

sanskrit: bhavitā vigrahaḥ so 'yaṃ tumulo lomaharṣaṇaḥ tasmāt sāṃgrāmikaṃ sarvaṃ kārayadhvam atandritāḥ
english: "This war that is coming will be tumultuous, hair-raising. Therefore, without delay, have all war preparations made."

sanskrit: śibirāṇi kurukṣetre kriyantāṃ vasudhādhipāḥ suparyāptāvakāśāni durādeyāni śatrubhiḥ
english: "Let camps be established at Kurukṣetra, O lords of the earth — with ample space, and made difficult for enemies to attack."

sanskrit: āsannajalakāṣṭhāni śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ acchedyāhāramārgāṇi ratnoccayacitāni ca vividhāyudhapūrṇāni patākādhvajavanti ca
english: "Close to water and firewood, by the hundreds and thousands; with supply lines that cannot be cut; piled with heaps of gems; filled with all manner of weapons; adorned with banners and pennants."

sanskrit: samāś ca teṣāṃ panthānaḥ kriyantāṃ nagarād bahiḥ prayāṇaṃ ghuṣyatām adya śvobhūta iti māciram
english: "And let level roads be made for them outside the city. Let the departure be announced today: 'tomorrow at dawn' — delay no longer."

sanskrit: te tatheti pratijñāya śvobhūte cakrire tathā hṛṣṭarūpā mahātmāno vināśāya mahīkṣitām
english: They pledged "So be it," and at the next dawn the great-souled warriors did as commanded, their faces joyful — though it was for the destruction of the kings of earth.

sanskrit: tatas te pārthivāḥ sarve tac chrutvā rājaśāsanam āsanebhyo mahārhebhya udatiṣṭhann amarṣitāḥ
english: Then all those kings, hearing the royal command, rose from their magnificent seats, burning with impatience.

sanskrit: bāhūn parighasaṃkāśān saṃspṛśantaḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ kāñcanāṅgadadīptāṃś ca candanāgarubhūṣitān
english: They stroked their arms — like iron bolts, blazing with golden armlets, adorned with sandalwood and aloe —

sanskrit: uṣṇīṣāṇi niyacchantaḥ puṇḍarīkanibhaiḥ karaiḥ antarīyottarīyāṇi bhūṣaṇāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: — tightening their turbans with lotus-like hands, arranging inner and outer garments and all their ornaments —

sanskrit: te rathān rathinaḥ śreṣṭhā hayāṃś ca hayakovidāḥ sajjayanti sma nāgāṃś ca nāgaśikṣāsu niṣṭhitāḥ
english: — the finest chariot-warriors prepared their chariots; those expert in horses prepared their horses; those trained in the lore of elephants prepared their elephants.

sanskrit: atha varmāṇi citrāṇi kāñcanāni bahūni ca vividhāni ca śastrāṇi cakruḥ sajjāni sarvaśaḥ
english: Then they readied their variegated armor of gold in great quantity, and all manner of weapons — making everything ready on every side.

sanskrit: padātayaś ca puruṣāḥ śastrāṇi vividhāni ca upajahruḥ śarīreṣu hemacitrāṇy anekaśaḥ
english: And foot-soldiers, men bearing all kinds of weapons, attached to their bodies gold-inlaid arms in manifold ways.

sanskrit: tad utsava ivodagraṃ saṃprahṛṣṭanarāvṛtam nagaraṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya bhāratāsīt samākulam
english: Like a great festival, the city of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son was thronged with delighted men, joyfully astir, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: janaughasalilāvarto rathanāgāśvamīnavān śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaḥ kośasaṃcayaratnavān
english: A whirlpool of the waters of human multitudes, filled with chariots, elephants, and horses as fish — resounding with conches and kettledrums — heaped with treasuries of gems —

sanskrit: citrābharaṇavarmormiḥ śastranirmalaphenavān prāsādamālādrivṛto rathyāpaṇamahāhradaḥ
english: — its waves the variegated ornaments and armor, its foam the gleaming weapons, its mountains the rows of palaces, its great lake the streets and markets —

sanskrit: yodhacandrodayodbhūtaḥ kururājamahārṇavaḥ adṛśyata tadā rājaṃś candrodaya ivārṇavaḥ
english: — stirred by the rising moon of warriors, the great ocean that was the Kuru king's realm appeared then, O king, like the ocean at the rising of the moon.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vāsudevasya tad vākyam anusmṛtya yudhiṣṭhiraḥ punaḥ papraccha vārṣṇeyaṃ kathaṃ mando 'bravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Recalling the words of Vāsudeva, Yudhiṣṭhira again questioned the Vṛṣṇi hero — how that foolish one had spoken thus:

sanskrit: asminn abhyāgate kāle kiṃ ca naḥ kṣamam acyuta kathaṃ ca vartamānā vai svadharmān na cyavemahi
english: "Now that this time has come upon us, what is proper for us, O Acyuta? And how, conducting ourselves rightly, shall we not swerve from our own dharma?"

sanskrit: duryodhanasya karṇasya śakuneḥ saubalasya ca vāsudeva matajño 'si mama sabhrātṛkasya ca
english: "You know the minds of Duryodhana, Karṇa, Śakuni the son of Subala, O Vāsudeva — and of me with my brothers as well."

sanskrit: vidurasyāpi te vākyaṃ śrutaṃ bhīṣmasya cobhayoḥ kuntyāś ca vipulaprajña prajñā kārtsnyena te śrutā
english: "The words of Vidura you have heard, and of both Bhīṣma as well; and the wisdom of Kuntī in its entirety has been heard by you, O one of vast intelligence."
